title: Safe Indexing and Options
goal: Learn how to query collections safely without panicking.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Afternoon: HashMap and Vec

sections.text: In Python or Java, accessing an out-of-bounds index throws an exception at runtime. Rust arrays and vectors panic if you index past the end with `v[i]`.

sections.code:
let v = vec![10, 20];
let second = v[1];
sections.caption: Direct indexing panics when out of bounds.

sections.text: To check bounds safely, call `.get(index)` on a vector or `.get(key)` on a `HashMap`. Both return an `Option<&T>` containing `Some(&value)` or `None`.

sections.caption: .get returns Option without panicking.

sections.text: Because `.get()` returns a reference `&T`, use `.copied()` or `.cloned()` on the `Option` if you need an owned copy of primitive types like integers.

sections.caption: .copied turns Option<&i32> into Option<i32>.

sections.text: Handling missing values and error unwrapping is explored in depth in the Option & Result deck later.

explanation: Learn how to query collections safely without panicking.
